function: Predicts DD-domain OTFS channel parameters (NBEATS) and designs the transmit pre-equalization matrix (DNN) so the UAV detects symbols without equalization, trading communication MSE against sensing CRLB (pp. 6-9).
system: Air-ground OTFS-ISAC downlink: single-antenna AP and single-antenna UAV UE, C=2 scatterers; 3 GHz, 15 kHz spacing, M=N=16, speeds up to 95 m/s; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: NBEATS predictor (supervised, MSE on ray-traced parameters) cascaded with a dual-branch residual DNN designer (unsupervised, weighted MSE+CRLB loss), each trained offline (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Wireless InSite ray tracing of UE trajectories gives delays, Doppler shifts, attenuations; 640 trajectory groups, 4:1 train/test split; fractional delay-Doppler model in the system model (pp. 3-4, 10).
test_conditions: Same ray-traced scene; trajectory groups split 4:1 for training and testing; transmit power swept 2-10 W and weight rho_C varied; no unseen scenario, speed, or band (pp. 10-12).
baselines: MMSE equalization at UE with perfect CSI (upper bound); pre-equalization with perfect CSI and with outdated CSI (same network); channel prediction versus LSTM, PatchTST, Autoformer (p. 10).
metrics: Channel-parameter MAPE (Fig. 4), communication MSE of demodulated symbols, sensing CRLB (velocity), MSE-CRLB trade-off versus weight, transmit power sweep, FLOPs at UE and AP (pp. 10-12).
complexity: FLOPs per inference at the AP: prediction 4.72e5, pseudo-inversion 2.68e8, pre-equalization network 4.04e8, frame total 6.74e8; UE needs 5x2^o MN FLOPs versus 16(MN)^3+... for equalization (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 10: "InSite [41] software to generate corresponding channels as the" dataset; Wireless InSite on a self-defined scene (AP at origin, C = 2 scatterers); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "which are divided into training and testing sets in a ratio of" 4:1; Fig. 6 sweeps transmit power. Held-out split and power sweep only; no unseen scene, speed, band, or number of paths.
q3_support: p. 10: "Minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization [45]:" (non-learned, Fig. 6 MSE) and "(PatchTST) [47], and Autoformer [48]" with LSTM [46] (learned, Fig. 4 MAPE); the learned comparison covers the prediction module only.
q4_support: p. 12: "Evaluated and validated by framework profilers (THOP for PyTorch and TensorFlow Profiler),"; FLOPs of each module and 6.74e8 per frame at the AP are given, and 5x2^o MN FLOPs at the UE.
q5_support: p. 10: "The dataset consists of 640 trajectory groups," generated by the authors with a commercial ray tracer; no code or data link or DOI appears in the paper.
notes: Area 4 over 5 by the tie-break order (OTFS before ISAC). AP and UE each have a single antenna (p. 3); this is admitted because OTFS works admit single-antenna links, and had the work been area 5 the system check would exclude it. q1: Wireless InSite is a commercial ray tracer on an author-defined scene, not a public dataset, so 0; the reviewer may reconsider. q3: LSTM, PatchTST, and Autoformer are compared for the prediction module only; the pre-equalization design has no learned baseline. Table I and Figs. 4-8 were checked as images (pp. 9-12). Title on p. 1 matches the DOI.
